newsitem.title: USA: Dole hits Clinton on drugs, money in first debate.
newsitem.headline: Dole hits Clinton on drugs, money in first debate.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole on Sunday accused President Bill Clinton of being soft on drug abuse and special interest money, drawing return fire in personal sparring at the U.S. campaign debate.

Dole, far back in the polls and in need of taking the offensive, went after Clinton on the issue of special interest money, saying: "When you're a few million short, you run out to Hollywood and pick up 2 to 4 million (dollars), and organized labor comes to Washington and puts 35 million (dollars) into the pot."

Clinton shot back by focussing on perceptions Dole is soft on the tobacco industry, saying: "Senator Dole's had some pretty harsh comments on special interests recently, but it wasn't me who opposed what we tried to do to save the lives of children who were subject to tobacco and then went to the tobacco growers and bragged about standing up to the government when we tried to stop the advertising, marketing and sales of tobacco to children."

Dole replied by accusing Clinton of presiding over a weakening in the fight against addictive drugs and a rise in drug use among the young, adding to a series of direct exchanges that gave the clash in Hartford's Bushnell Theater some of the flavor of a real argument. The two speakers addressed each directly from lecterns a few feet apart.
Clinton countered by accusing Dole of opposing a crime bill bill that included the death penalty for drug kingpins, but reserved his strongest fire for a personal sidelight.

"Let my remind you that my family has suffered from drug abuse," he said, referring to his half-brother Roger, a recovering drug abuser. "I know what it's like to see somebody you love nearly lose their life. And I hate drugs, senator."
